original-en.context: EDMUND. Thou, Nature, art my goddess; to thy law My services are bound. Wherefore should I Stand in the plague of custom, and permit The curiosity of nations to deprive me? For that I am some twelve or fourteen moonshines Lag of a brother? Why bastard? Wherefore base? When my dimensions are as well compact, My mind as generous, and my shape as true As honest madam’s issue? Why brand they us With base? With baseness? bastardy? Base, base? Who, in the lusty stealth of nature, take More composition and fierce quality Than doth within a dull stale tired bed Go to the creating a whole tribe of fops Got ’tween asleep and wake? Well then, Legitimate Edgar, I must have your land: Our father’s love is to the bastard Edmund As to the legitimate: fine word: legitimate! Well, my legitimate, if this letter speed, And my invention thrive, Edmund the base Shall top the legitimate. I grow, I prosper. Now, gods, stand up for bastards!

modern-en.context: EDMUND. You, Nature, are my goddess. To your law my services are bound. Why should I stand under the plague of custom and let the prudery of nations rob me? Because I'm some twelve or fourteen months younger than a brother? Why bastard? Why base? When my body is as well-made, my mind as generous, and my shape as true as honest madam's offspring? Why do they brand us with base? With baseness? Bastardy? Base, base? We who, in the lusty stealth of nature, take more composition and fierce quality than is poured—within a dull, stale, tired bed—into the creating of a whole tribe of fops, got between asleep and wake? Well then, legitimate Edgar, I must have your lands. Our father's love is the same to bastard Edmund as to the legitimate. Fine word—legitimate! Well, my legitimate, if this letter does its work and my invention thrives, base Edmund shall top the legitimate. I grow, I prosper. Now, gods, stand up for bastards!
